source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-24:30 (tools/video_draft.py transcript CWsZxo1pB6Y --start 0 --end 1470), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 24:30 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of mqZsj4Vg2Es it repeats.

ideas.claim: Variable Chaser is good mostly because it is a three-mana 2/3 flier with prowess; its Ark of Fortune half (each player discards and draws seven) is risky because the opponent gets seven cards with all their mana open.
ideas.quote: making each player discard their hand to draw seven um is pretty risky cuz giving your opponent seven cards and then they'll have all of their mana untapped
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Variable Chaser against other rares and 3-drop fliers; skill-split.

ideas.claim: Hapatra, the Desert Fang over No Admittance in P1p1: a two-for-one (3/3 plus a kill once the graveyard has a card) that is also splashable; a mono-coloured card is only a close second.
ideas.quote: I think it's enough better than No Admittance that it's worth taking.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA by top drafters for both; within-deck value per game in hand.

ideas.claim: A gold card with a basic landcycler in the deck is easier to splash: cycle the landcycler, the big card in the graveyard turns Hapatra on, and the cycler fetches the basic that makes the splash.
ideas.quote: if you're playing like any black deck, you have the Hepatra. You play like an Apex Witch Stalker, you cycle it, that puts a big mana value card in your graveyard, and then you get your forest, and you can play Hapatra even if you're not playing black green specifically.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Hapatra in decks with 0, 1, 2 basic landcyclers when it is a splash card.

ideas.claim: Removal in a colour you are not playing is passed in favour of the graveyard engine card ('we don't have to be a green deck'); early picks go to power and synergy, not to the on-colour removal count.
ideas.quote: I think I'm going to try this rewrite regrets thing and see if I can make a black potential graveyard deck work.
ideas.test_idea: Pick order of Rewrite Regrets versus removal among 60%+ drafters; GIH WR of Rewrite Regrets by number of self-mill cards.

ideas.claim: Proft, Consulting Detective gets better with surveil effects, and Empower Jace cards that tick down by one feed it.
ideas.quote: a lot of your empower Jace cards might not get all the way to three. So you can tick down minus one, get your prof going.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Proft by count of surveil/Empower Jace cards in the deck.

ideas.claim: Prefer power level over the on-colour land early: 'I'm still taking power level cards', so the blue-black dual goes behind Proft and Amphisbaena.
ideas.quote: I think there a blue black land. I'm not going to take that here. I'm still taking power level cards.
ideas.test_idea: Pick order of non-basic lands versus strong playables at P1p3 for 60%+ drafters; value of a dual land taken before pick 4.

ideas.claim: Mabel, Bitter Recluse is a good defensive body that also answers counters (a Jace token, +1/+1 counters), preferred over an off-plan gold card.
ideas.quote: that's pretty good as a defensive body as well for maybe my defensive black green blue kind of space deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Mabel, Bitter Recluse.

ideas.claim: Seeing cards of a colour pair arrive in pack 1 pick 4 to 5 is the first sign that blue-black is open.
ideas.quote: Okay, it's looking like blue black is open which is nice.
ideas.test_idea: Whether cards of the colour pair seen at picks 4-6 predict the pair's win rate for the drafter (signal strength by pick number).

ideas.claim: Take the rare (Dark Matter Manipulator) for the experience rather than the uncommon in the same pack, staying in black.
ideas.quote: I'm going to try taking the rare. We'll get some experience with the rare.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Dark Matter Manipulator vs Paradox Shaper vs Undulating Witness.

ideas.claim: Clash of Elements is very strong but not worth splashing for; he stays in colours and gets Keeper of the Quiet Hour later.
ideas.quote: Clash of Elements is very strong, but I don't really want necessarily want to go splashing this direction.
ideas.test_idea: Splash value of a strong gold or off-colour card versus its GIH WR gap to the on-colour alternative.

ideas.claim: Only take one effect of a type: with one removal spell like Silence the Echo already worth having, the second is passed for card filtering.
ideas.quote: I think I only really want one of this type of effect even though it's like pretty efficient at times
ideas.test_idea: Diminishing returns for duplicate sorcery-speed removal spells in a deck (marginal win rate by copy count).

ideas.claim: A land that fixes a possible splash is worth taking over a mediocre playable early (white-black dual over Inspired Tethermage).
ideas.quote: I might take the meticulous commons though because maybe I would want to splash white for something.
ideas.test_idea: Value of an early dual land by the number of splash-worthy cards that arrive later.

ideas.claim: Undulating Witness is a flier with basic landcycling that works with a splash and Hapatra.
ideas.quote: It's a flyer. It has basic land cycling to work with my Hepatra or if I wanted to splash white or something like that.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Undulating Witness by number of splash colours.

ideas.claim: Proft, Sinister Mastermind is a scary card with a full graveyard and can be discarded for early interaction when it cannot be cast.
ideas.quote: I can discard it for some early interaction.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Proft, Sinister Mastermind by graveyard size (turn of play).

ideas.claim: Cards of a colour coming back late in the pack (green at P1p11) suggest the colour is open; he moves back towards it.
ideas.quote: We have gotten back some of these green cards, so that does make me think that maybe that deck will be open.
ideas.test_idea: Whether late (wheeled or low-pick) cards of a colour at picks 9-12 predict that colour's later flow.

ideas.claim: A pack of blue-black cards coming last (Theorix Metamage as the last real card) means blue-black is fairly open, so a deck needs little splashing.
ideas.quote: Blue black is looking fairly open. I don't mind passing up on the like three mana mana rock
ideas.test_idea: As the signal claim above; also pick order of Murmuring Volume versus on-colour playables.

ideas.claim: Paradox Shaper is a late-game card worth exactly one copy in a self-mill deck: mill the whole deck and stack it; slow, but fine if the deck has early defence.
ideas.quote: I really want to have one in this deck, I think, as kind of a nice cool late game card to maybe assemble.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Paradox Shaper (single copy) in decks with at least five self-mill sources.

ideas.claim: Hapatra, the Desert Frost (stun counter, four-mana tempo play) matters most when the four-drop slot is empty; he still takes Paradox Shaper first.
ideas.quote: How's my four drops slot looking? A little bit empty right now.
ideas.test_idea: Curve-slot value: GIH WR of a card by whether the deck already has 2+ cards at its mana value.

ideas.claim: A fixing land can be the pick when the pack holds nothing for the deck; he takes Room of Refuge over several playables and expects Murmuring Volume or another land to wheel.
ideas.quote: I think I'm just going to take the land here. There's nothing crazy for me here.
ideas.test_idea: Pick order of Room of Refuge among 60%+ drafters; wheel rate of Murmuring Volume.

ideas.claim: All three Echoverse cards still in the pack means there is no signal from the pair; a missing one would tell which colour pair was taken.
ideas.quote: I don't get any information cuz there's all three still in the pack.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable with public data (the card removed upstream is not in the data).

ideas.claim: Multiply by Zero is removal for any creature in his deck's matchup space except ones with +1/+1 counters or a boost; with no counters in his own deck it hits everything in a self-mirror.
ideas.quote: Target creature has base power and toughness 0 until end of turn. So if they have a plus and plus encounter on it, it's going to be a little bit tricky.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Multiply by Zero against opponents' counter-heavy decks; compared to Last Gasp.

ideas.claim: A splash colour is chosen by what it brings: green for Hapatra and later Bestial Incursion rather than white for Surgical Precision or Generous Revival.
ideas.quote: if I do need to splash, I could splash like white instead of green for this sort of card, but I think Hpatra is going to be amazing in my deck.
ideas.test_idea: Compare the deck win rate of the two splash choices by the splash cards' GIH WR.

ideas.claim: Jace, Reality Sculptor is good in a stable board position: plus one draws a card and it can take over; it is expensive but worth taking when the pack has nothing else for the deck.
ideas.quote: he's like plus one to draw a card a lot of the time. So, if you're in a stable board position, he can kind of take over the game
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Jace, Reality Sculptor by deck speed (average mana value).

ideas.claim: A dual land that fixes the splash colour for the splash bomb is taken over a marginal Empower Jace card.
ideas.quote: I'm just going to take the green black land. It makes it a little bit easier to play this Hatra.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Hapatra by number of green sources; pick order of Formidable Commons.

ideas.claim: Terminal Criticism and the like are sideboard cards for best-of-three that are not main-deck material.
ideas.quote: There's a whole cycle of these cards that are sideboard cards essentially.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable on Bo1 Premier data (sideboard cards).

ideas.claim: A two-mana 1/3 that makes small creatures unblockable is only 'okay'; Blessed Ghoul is preferred in a self-mill deck because it comes back from the graveyard.
ideas.quote: I think I might just take the blessed ghoul though. I have a lot of self mill.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Blessed Ghoul by self-mill count (he later cuts it).

ideas.claim: Null Summoner is the best card in his deck and came seventh pick in pack two, so a strong gold card can arrive very late when its pair is not being drafted.
ideas.quote: this card is going to be the best card in my deck. And I got it seventh pick in pack two.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Null Summoner; pick-number distribution of gold cards of the pair.

ideas.claim: With dual lands for two possible splashes in the pool he commits to only one splash colour and keeps taking power; Theoretical Necromancer gives an extra resource when milled.
ideas.quote: I might just only try to splash one of the colors depending on which one of these seems like it'll be better for my deck.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate of one splash vs two given the number of fixers.

ideas.claim: A deck that plays mostly at sorcery speed should not take a cheap counter spell; he already has enough one- and two-drops, so a flashback card for self-mill beats Icy Reception.
ideas.quote: My deck doesn't really hold its mana up particularly well because I'm mostly playing at sorcery speed
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Icy Reception by deck's instant-speed share; pick order against Bestial Incursion.

ideas.claim: Bestial Incursion (self-mill, flashback a 4/4 trampler) is worth it as the second green splash card; it makes green over white 'a no-brainer'.
ideas.quote: once I got a beastial incursion, splashing green over white is just kind of a no-brainer
ideas.test_idea: Splash value by the second splash card in a colour (marginal win rate of the 2nd vs 1st splash card).

ideas.claim: Prefer the removal spell to extra card draw when the pool has plenty of draw; Multiply by Zero over Last Gasp and Mindseeker Oculus.
ideas.quote: I have plenty of card draw. I've got good value. I just want more kill spells
ideas.test_idea: Marginal value of the nth card-draw card versus the nth removal spell by deck composition.

ideas.claim: Theorix Charm is the on-colour blue-black card that does everything (counter, -2/-2, mill three and draw); two copies are taken over Tinybones.
ideas.quote: This card's great though. I can mill three and draw or I can think minus two.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Theorix Charm vs Tinybones, Pocket Nuisance.

ideas.claim: Splash only 'the best of the best': a splash card in a pack with Null Summoner is declined.
ideas.quote: only want to splash the best of the best.
ideas.test_idea: Deck value of a splash by the splash card's GIH WR edge over the deck's 23rd on-colour card.

ideas.claim: Prefer the graveyard-synergy card (Gallia) over a good counter spell (Countersculpt) when the plan is graveyard value.
ideas.quote: I'd rather just get more cards that work with my graveyard. That's kind of my current plan.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Gallia vs Countersculpt; he later wheels Countersculpt at P3p12.

ideas.claim: Unsummon is a nice interactive spell to have exactly one copy of; a second Theoretical Necromancer is not needed because one already covers the Generous Revival role.
ideas.quote: unsummon's a nice a little interactive spell to have one copy of I think.
ideas.test_idea: Duplicate penalty for Theoretical Necromancer; GIH WR of Unsummon.

ideas.claim: The second fixing land (Room of Refuge) is taken over Icy Reception or Infinite Coursework because 'I just like getting my mana' better with a splash planned.
ideas.quote: I just like getting my mana a little bit
ideas.test_idea: Pick order of Room of Refuge at P3p7 for splash decks; win rate by number of Room of Refuge copies.

ideas.claim: Counter spells and draw spells that do not fit his deck (Precise Redaction, Sphinx's Approach) are treated as sideboard cards; no pick is announced.
ideas.quote: This is like a sideboard counter spell. I'm not going to be able to use it though.
ideas.test_idea: none (no engine claim)

ideas.claim: Wheeling Mindseeker Oculus, Way of the Mind Sculptor and Last Gasp in a pack of 14 shows how much of the pack comes back in this format; he calls wheeling Mindseeker Oculus 'wild'.
ideas.quote: I kind of wield everything.
ideas.test_idea: Wheel rates by card at pick 9 of a 14-card pack, by colour pair (what the engine's wheel expectation should be).

ideas.claim: Late picks of cheap card draw (Protege's Awakening, Void Extrapolator) are fine value even when not needed.
ideas.quote: Perfect. I got a little bit more card draw anyway.
ideas.test_idea: none

ideas.claim: He says Way of the Necromancer is not great ('I'm not like in love with that') and plays neither copy.
ideas.quote: I don't think way of necromancer is great.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Way of the Necromancer.

ideas.claim: The deck builder starts at 47 cards (auto-filled with 14 basics) and he makes seven cuts, preferring to cut the more expensive cards and keep a cheaper curve.
ideas.quote: I have to make seven cuts though. ... I usually like to lean towards cutting the more expensive cards
ideas.test_idea: Cut order of the builder against 17Lands deck data: does the cut card by mana value predict win rate.

ideas.claim: A single Forest with several green sources (Formidable Commons, Room of Refuge x2) gives about six green sources for three splash cards, which he calls totally enough.
ideas.quote: So six green sources for one, two, three cards. That's totally enough.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of a splash card by number of sources (4/5/6) for single-pip cards.

ideas.claim: A splash card that does not work with the graveyard plan (Compel Brutality) is cut even when it is removal; he plays only splash cards that mill-synergise.
ideas.quote: Maybe I'll cut the compelled brutality because it doesn't like synergize with the graveyard.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate with and without a splash removal spell that has no synergy.

ideas.claim: Cutting Protege's Awakening: a big card-draw spell with no Empower Jace synergy is cut when the deck already has card advantage.
ideas.quote: I'd rather just uh it doesn't like I don't have tons of synergies with like empower J. It's just like a big draw card draw spell and I'm getting plenty of card advantage from other stuff
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Protege's Awakening by deck's other card-advantage count.

ideas.claim: At 16 creatures he cuts one: with enough early plays, the more expensive (or weaker) creature goes and the deck keeps a cheaper curve.
ideas.quote: My creature count is at 16. I think I can cut a creature here. ... I'd rather just have a cheaper curve.
ideas.test_idea: Creature count and curve: deck win rate by creature count (14-17) at constant quality.

ideas.claim: He might drop the splash if the playables are there, but the splash bomb (Hapatra) justifies it; the deck stays flexible across the five rounds.
ideas.quote: Maybe I decide not to splash because I do have plenty of playables, but I think Hapatra is going to be really really strong.
ideas.test_idea: Splash value of one bomb with a conditional effect (graveyard) versus a deck without the splash.
